lines: The House of the Hollow Star
the Hanging Ring, hung from the cavern roof round Zhaelvorn; a silk lift on the cavern floor under each manor carries you up
A small six-eyed cave cat with soft violet glow in its fur. It purrs like falling water.
Layered dark silk robes with silver thread, a deep hood and a cloak the colour of the cavern.
Duskwing folds its wings and drops on the ground before you: a ring of shadow strikes every foe around.
the Headland Row, on the shore east of the harbour past the Nautilus dock, each lighthouse at the water's edge
A loyal, clever sea dog, after the dog of The Mysterious Island (1874). He swims like a seal.
A dark naval coat with brass buttons, a captain's cap, a sea scarf and boots: the look of the books, never a film's.
The Terror lunges forward at full power: everything in its path is struck and thrown aside.
the Villa Road, on the hills north-west of Florence above the Porta al Prato
A small clockwork lion cub of carved wood and gilt, after the walking lion Leonardo built for the King of France in 1515.
A painter-inventor's long robe, soft cap, a leather apron and a satchel for the notebooks.
The wings beat down hard: a gust like a falcon's stoop hits every foe in a line ahead.
🌊 The end of the jetty. The sea runs all the way to the south, over the Deep where the Nautilus sails; Stromboli smokes far out in the bay, and behind you the lamp turns slowly in its tower.

A beam of black wood bound in silver, held out over the city on an arm of living rock. Cave wyverns roost on perches like this; from here you can see every spire of Zhaelvorn.

The door sticks. Try again in a moment.
Nothing happens. Perhaps there is a clue somewhere else in the house.
The way back is behind you.
You climb back up, and the way closes quietly behind you.
🫧 The bathysphere. The hatch closes, the water rises past the glass, and a cable draws you out under the headland. You come up beside the Nautilus dock.
You look into the dark water. Your strength comes back to you, all of it, cool and clear.
You drink from the Moonwell. Every hurt closes, and for a while you breathe as easily as the moths that live here.
Inside the chest: dry charts of every ocean, a sextant, and a tin of ship's biscuits. You eat one, and feel ready for anything.
You turn the crank of the model flying machine. The gears hum all through the house, and you feel quick on your feet.
You open the codex of the cellar: drawings of machines never built, and a page in his hand about the flight of birds. You come away clear-headed and strong.
A note in a Matron's hand, tucked in a book: "What the Hollow Star keeps, it keeps behind the seventh book of the scrying shelf, the one bound in silver that is never read."
The scrying shelf. Which book do you pull?
The first book, bound in black
The seventh book, bound in silver
The last book, bound in red
The thickest book, bound in spider silk
The seventh book tilts with a click. The whole shelf swings inward on silent hinges, and cold air rises from a stair going down.
Carved round the parlour hearth: "Teal for the deep, violet for the dark, white for the star. In that order, the stone will lift."
Three great glowcaps stand here, teal, violet and white. Which order do you touch them in?
The third cap brightens softly. A silk lift lowers from a hidden shaft in the ceiling and carries you up to a garden no one has seen for a hundred years.
The Library of the Extraordinary Voyages
The last line in the captain's log on the library desk: "Mobilis in mobili. When the wheel is set south-south-west, the sea will let you in."
The great ship's wheel of the Chart Room. Which heading do you set?
The wheel turns with a deep clank. Behind the chart cabinet a hatch rolls open onto an iron stair, and you smell the sea.
Pencilled on the cabin's star map: "The Southern Cross points to the chest. Look there, not at the Pole."
The brass telescope. Where do you turn it?
As the telescope comes round to the Southern Cross, the floor plate under your feet sinks slowly into a brass-lined strongroom.
A notebook on the library desk, in mirror-writing that you read in the glass beside it: "The panel of the studio opens to the word the city of the river says backwards: ONRA."
A painted panel, with letters set into its frame. Which word do you spell?
The letters sink one by one. The panel slides aside with a sound of wooden wheels, and behind it the gears of the house are turning.
A riddle framed on the wall: "Three stand round the water. Turn all three to face it, and the water will go down to show you the way."
The fountain and its three small statues. What do you do?
Turn all three to face the fountain
As the third statue turns, the fountain drains with a long gurgle and its basin sinks into steps going down into a candlelit cellar.
The Hall of the Hollow Star

🔭 The stars over Florence. The Moon's pale ashen light (Leonardo was the first to explain it: sunlight bounced off the Earth), Jupiter, and the Milky Way across the hills.
